neighbours.label: Abstract state/attribute noun (status, health, conduct, problems) completing a modified noun phrase about a condition or person, usually where 'of' or a complement is expected next; strongest in disease/health and social-policy text
fire: Hospitals are now required to report the vaccination status of every patient admitted to the ward.
After the diagnosis, her doctors tracked the overall health of the whole family for several years.
The council investigated the professional conduct of two officers who had been on the night shift.
Researchers found that children with chronic asthma often develop other respiratory problems later in life.
A new law will make it harder to verify the immigration status of seasonal farm workers.
Over the decades the nurse monitored the mental health of soldiers returning from the northern front.
The lab confirmed that most of the isotopes in the sample were radioactive and decayed within days.
Nobody questioned the legal standing of the contract until the tuberculosis outbreak closed the clinic.
quiet: Hospitals are now required to wash every surface in the ward before the morning round begins.
After the move, her cousins repainted the kitchen and planted tomatoes along the whole fence.
The council approved a budget for two new buses that would run on the night shift.
Children with chronic asthma often prefer swimming to running when the weather turns cold.
A new bakery will open next to the bus station, selling bread to seasonal farm workers.
Over the decades the nurse collected stamps from every country along the northern front.
The lab confirmed that the sample was blue, heavy, and stored in a locked drawer by the door.
Nobody questioned the paint colour until the football match ended and the stadium emptied.

notes: 10x pilot (concept-maps/tenx, census arm): label and 16 sentences written by a fresh Sonnet 5.5 subagent from a packet (card + all-pole band samples + concept-census evidence (which concepts and domains selected the pole)); no probes. An Opus gate checked rule-level items only (8 + 8, 0 overlap with census and probe text, near misses free of the declared trigger) and edited nothing. Labeller's note: Strong activations are heterogeneous: head nouns like status, health, conduct, problems, system, centre that sit before an expected 'of' or complement; the census shows a clear disease-domain preference (70% of diseases vs 0% of objects). Label is a tentative grammatical-plus-topic hypothesis; the band samples show many weak off-topic tokens, so expect partial coverage.
